# Homeowner questions we saved

Answers from a home improvement store's help pages, printed for the house binder.

## Can I remove the wall between my kitchen and dining room?

Many walls can come out, but some hold up the house. Have a professional look at it before you start, and check whether the work needs a permit.

## What size circuit does a new electric dryer need?

Large appliances like dryers usually need a circuit of their own. Check the appliance's nameplate or manual, and have an electrician install the outlet.

## What temperature should my water heater be set to?

Follow the manufacturer's recommendation, and turn it down if you have young children or older adults in the house.

## How do I find a good contractor?

Ask neighbors for names, get three written quotes, check the license and insurance, and look at recent jobs. Avoid anyone who wants a large payment up front.

## When should I replace my roof?

Asphalt shingles last about 20 to 25 years. Curling, bald spots, missing shingles and leaks are signs that it is time.

## How can I lower my heating bill?

Seal air leaks around doors and windows, add attic insulation, change the furnace filter, and set the thermostat a few degrees lower when you are away.

## How far can a deck joist span?

Joist spans depend on the size of the lumber, its spacing, the kind of wood and the load. Use the span tables in your local building code, or ask at the lumber yard.

## How deep should deck footings be?

Footing depth depends on your local frost line and your soil. Ask your building department what is required in your area.
